In its format war, VHS competed against.why: The VHS-Betamax format war is one of the best-known stories in consumer technology; Wikipedia has an article on it and the pair is named together thousands of times.

sources.quote: The videotape format war was a period of competition or "format war" of incompatible models of consumer-level analog videocassette formats and video cassette recorders (VCRs) in the late 1970s and the 1980s, mainly involving the Betamax and VHS (Video Home System) formats.
It was one of the main competitors in the videotape format war against its primary rival, VHS.

The high-definition optical disc format war was a market competition between two optical disc standards for distributing high-definition video: Blu-ray Disc, backed by Sony, and HD DVD, backed by Toshiba.
